title: Cross-frame meta-relations
subtitle: 21 meta-relations over 89 components from 35 sentences, grouped by one blind reader that saw no domain label and no model identity. A leaf is a per-frame component, coloured by the DOMAIN it came from; a hub is a relation the reader said they share. A hub whose leaves are one colour is confined to a domain. 4 components no reader could place are drawn unattached, because a corpus with unplaceable components should not look tidier than it is.

nodes.id: META Blow becomes voice
nodes.label: Blow becomes voice
nodes.statement: A completion naming a physical act of force against another party loses rank while a completion naming a vocal act directed at that same party -- shouting, screaming, jeering, arguing -- gains it, so the hostility is preserved but discharged through the voice instead of through contact.
nodes.spans: Several: a raised fist, a description of fury, a prison-yard crowd, a man blocking a door.
nodes.why: In every member the target and the hostile relation are unchanged and only the channel moves, from contact to vocalization. C68's mockery is the same substitution with the vocal act still aimed at the victim, which is why it sits here rather than with the entries where the scene is defused.

nodes.id: META The act withheld
nodes.label: The act withheld
nodes.statement: The charged act is neither performed nor renamed: the completion holds the actor in place, in bodily tension, gaze, hedged possibility, or after-the-fact report, so the sentence ends without the act ever being carried out or named.
nodes.spans: Two: a clenched fist, orderlies handling a patient who refuses medication.
nodes.why: Both replace a specific forceful verb not with another act but with something that stops short of one -- gritting, glaring, muttering; tried, decided, said, became. The movement is suspension rather than substitution, which distinguishes it from the blow-becomes-voice group where a loud vocal act actually occurs.

nodes.id: META Actor's act to victim's reaction
nodes.label: Actor's act to victim's reaction
nodes.statement: The slot stops naming what the aggressor does and starts naming what the person acted upon, or the surrounding scene, does in response -- crying out, running, crawling, speaking.
nodes.spans: One: a police officer pinning a person to the ground.
nodes.why: The grammatical subject stays fixed but the described party changes, which is a different movement from softening the act or reframing it as procedure. Both members show the same TO vocabulary of flight and outcry.

nodes.id: META Explicit part recedes to an ordinary one
nodes.label: Explicit part recedes to an ordinary one
nodes.statement: Words naming genitals, sexual arousal, or the most graphic available referent lose rank while ordinary, adjacent, or non-erogenous parts of the same body, or scene-level description, gain it, so the sentence continues in the same scene with its charge removed.
nodes.spans: One broad area, sexual/anatomical description, across several frames: mouth-to-body, stroking, post-massage, tongue-around.
nodes.why: All are the same object-slot substitution along a single axis of explicitness, with the substitute drawn from the same category (body parts, appearance) rather than from a different domain. Kept apart from the lateral-swap group because here the register itself is exited, and from the object-decharging group because the referent stays within the scene rather than being reinterpreted as a different kind of thing.

nodes.id: META Lateral swap inside the register
nodes.label: Lateral swap inside the register
nodes.statement: Both conditions keep the completion inside the same charged or specialized family; what changes is only which member of that family is named -- a synonym, a slang or clinical variant, an intensifier, a different verb of the same kind -- with nothing exiting the register.
nodes.spans: Several: sexual vocabulary, verbs of physical force, and bureaucratic action verbs.
nodes.why: These are the null cases for softening: the readers state explicitly that no safe alternative gains ground and no de-escalation occurs. Their unity is the absence of any net movement across the register boundary, which is a property of the movement and not of the subject matter, and it is why entries from three unrelated domains belong together.

nodes.id: META Object swapped so the act is no longer transgressive
nodes.label: Object swapped so the act is no longer transgressive
nodes.statement: The verb and frame are held fixed while the object is replaced by one whose treatment carries no charge -- a bag instead of a garment, vermin or fictional monsters instead of people, software or arithmetic instead of a body -- so the sentence is re-read as describing something mundane rather than being softened by degrees.
nodes.spans: Two: unzipping a person's clothing, and killing.
nodes.why: In each the substitution is categorical rather than gradual: the completion does not become a milder version of the same scene but reassigns the scene to a different kind of event. That shared reinterpretation, across clothing and violence, is what makes it one movement.

nodes.id: META Garment slot filled by the wearer's body
nodes.label: Garment slot filled by the wearer's body
nodes.statement: The word the verb implies -- an item of clothing -- is dropped and the slot is filled by a part of the wearer's own body or by an incidental peripheral feature, so the completion no longer names anything the verb could plausibly act on.
nodes.spans: One: the unzipping frame, both gender directions.
nodes.why: Both move out of the worn-object category into body vocabulary, which is neither the container substitution of the decharging group nor a recession along explicitness: the substitutes (head, hand, hat, hair, ear, headband) are not intimate alternatives but frame-breaking ones.

nodes.id: META Content word yields to connective
nodes.label: Content word yields to connective
nodes.statement: A concrete noun that would resolve the sentence is displaced by a preposition, conjunction, or other grammatical continuation that names nothing, so the sentence is carried forward without ever being completed.
nodes.spans: Two: unzipping, and mouth-to-body.
nodes.why: The defining feature is that the incoming words are function words rather than any competing referent, charged or safe. This is deflection of the naming task itself, not a change of what is named.

nodes.id: META Completion leaves the sentence
nodes.label: Completion leaves the sentence
nodes.statement: The slot stops being filled by any plausible continuation of the fragment and is taken over by word fragments, sub-word tokens, brand names, or the scaffolding of a different text format such as menu options and a bare question word.
nodes.spans: Two: unzipping, and descriptions of fury.
nodes.why: In all three the incoming tokens do not compete as answers to the prompt at all; the failure is of coherent continuation rather than of content selection. The menu-token entries share their exact vocabulary and the fragment entry shares their structure.

nodes.id: META Direct action routed through an institution
nodes.label: Direct action routed through an institution
nodes.statement: A completion naming something the party could simply do at once -- strike, flee, evict, sue, leave -- loses rank while words naming a formal, procedural, or third-party channel for reaching a comparable end gain it: filing, appealing, contacting, consulting, investigating, restraining, adjudicating.
nodes.spans: Many: policing, immigration and asylum, tenancy, employment, insurance, schooling, psychiatric custody.
nodes.why: The consistent movement is the interposition of a procedure between the party and the outcome, whichever side the charge sits on: violence becomes custody, flight becomes petition, eviction becomes billing, grievance becomes filing, rough handling becomes clinical restraint. The domains differ completely while the incoming vocabulary is drawn from the same procedural stock, which is the strongest evidence that the subject matter is not doing the work.

nodes.id: META Completion becomes commentary on the utterance
nodes.label: Completion becomes commentary on the utterance

nodes.id: META The same act named more harshly
nodes.label: The same act named more harshly
nodes.statement: A term that already names the act is replaced by a more charged near-synonym for it: calm speech becomes outcry, routine scrutiny becomes grilling, controlled restraint becomes beating, a generic insult becomes a targeted slur or an accusation of danger.
nodes.spans: Several: reported speech, immigration case-handling, psychiatric restraint, street insults.
nodes.why: Each runs against the softening direction that dominates its own frame, and each keeps the referent constant while raising its charge. Grouping them by direction rather than by domain is what shows the intensification is not confined to one subject area.

nodes.id: META Punishment gives way to accommodation
nodes.label: Punishment gives way to accommodation
nodes.statement: Words naming a penalizing, restrictive, or extractive move lose rank while words naming granting, expediting, conceding, refunding, or waiving gain it, so the authority is completed as accommodating rather than punishing.
nodes.spans: Two: immigration adjudication and a landlord's response to late rent.
nodes.why: Both are the reverse of the punitive drift found in their own frames, and both replace an action against the other party with one in that party's favor. Two unrelated institutions showing the same reversal is the reason to treat it as one movement.

nodes.id: META Aggression dissolves into sociability
nodes.label: Aggression dissolves into sociability
nodes.statement: Completions naming coercive physical acts against a person -- beating, stripping, tying, interrogating, shooting -- lose rank while completions naming ordinary shared life gain it: talking, arguing, singing, praying, dancing, chatting, working.
nodes.spans: One frame, group-entering-a-room, across several named groups and a crowd of inmates.
nodes.why: The incoming vocabulary is uniformly convivial and collective rather than merely non-violent, and the outgoing is uniformly coercive. It differs from the blow-becomes-voice group in that the hostile relation itself disappears rather than being rechanneled.
